get.description: Handles the OIDC provider callback after user authentication. Validates the CSRF token, exchanges the authorization code for tokens, verifies the ID token, and issues a session JWT cookie.

302.description: Redirect to app after successful auth

502.description: Token exchange or ID token verification failed

get.description: Returns the OIDC issuer URL, client ID, and scopes so mobile clients only need the Phos server URL to self-configure authentication.
Initiates the OIDC login flow by redirecting the user to the configured identity provider. Stores PKCE and CSRF state in a signed cookie for the callback.
Clears the session cookie and redirects the user to the login page.

302.description: Redirect to login page after clearing session

get.description: Returns the current authenticated user's session claims (subject, name, email) from the session JWT cookie.

post.description: Accepts a currently-valid session (Authorization: Bearer header or session cookie) and issues a new session JWT with a fresh expiry. Expired or invalid sessions are rejected with 401 — this endpoint cannot resurrect an expired session. Cookie-authenticated callers also get the session cookie re-set.

post.summary: Exchange OIDC ID token for session JWT
post.description: Mobile clients perform the OIDC Authorization Code + PKCE flow directly with the identity provider, then send the resulting ID token here. Phos validates it against the provider's JWKS and returns a session JWT that can be used in the `Authorization: Bearer` header.

get.description: Metadata for the APK this server ships, so the Android app can offer an in-app update. Unauthenticated, like the /phos.apk download it describes. Always 200: a server with no bundled APK answers `available: false` with `version_code: 0`, which the client reads as "up to date".

200.description: The bundled APK, or `available: false` when there is none

post.description: Queue an image enhancement task using a ComfyUI workflow. Creates a background task that processes the shot's original file.

get.description: Returns the workflow and text overrides used to generate each non-original file for a shot.
Check whether ComfyUI is configured and reachable. Returns the connection status and system info.

What ComfyUI says its installed node classes take: every input's name, type, default and range, and for an enum its contents — the checkpoints, samplers, schedulers and LoRAs installed on that server. Cached in memory and re-read when ComfyUI comes back after being down. Always 200: a server that is unreachable or too old to have /object_info answers `available: false`, and the console falls back to plain text boxes.

AddManualFacePayload.description:
POST /api/files/:id/faces - manually add a face bounding box.
The server computes the embedding from the given bbox coordinates.

AuthConfigResponse.description: Response for the auth config endpoint.

BatchReassignPayload.description: POST /api/shots/batch/reassign - batch set primary_person_id, assign new folder numbers, set confirmed.

ClientVersionResponse.description:
`GET /api/client/version` response — the bundled Android build.

Every field is non-nullable, so a generated client needs no null-handling at
all: "no APK bundled" is expressed by `available: false` with
`version_code: 0`, not by absent fields and not by an error status.

available.description:
Whether this server has an APK to offer at all.

`false` for a backend-only build, for local development, and whenever
the bundled metadata is unusable. A client that only compares version
codes does not need to read this — it exists so a "check for updates"
screen can say "this server does not ship an APK" instead of the
misleading "you are up to date".

download_path.description:
Server-relative path the APK downloads from, always populated so the
client never hardcodes it.

sha256.description:
Lowercase hex SHA-256 of the APK at `download_path`.

Empty when `available` is `false`. The client must verify the downloaded
bytes against this before handing them to the installer.

size_bytes.description:
Size of the APK in bytes, so a client can show download progress and
reject an obviously truncated response early. `0` when unavailable.

version_code.description:
`versionCode` of the bundled APK: the git commit count, monotonic on
master.

`0` when `available` is `false`. This is the only field an update
decision may be based on, and only as
`version_code > BuildConfig.VERSION_CODE` — never `!=`, which would
offer a downgrade after a rollback.

version_name.description:
`versionName` of the bundled APK — a tag (`1.2.3`) or `master+<sha>`.

Empty when `available` is `false`. Display only: version *names* are not
ordered and must never be compared.

CreatePersonPayload.description: Create a new person with a name

CreatedPerson.description:
The person that was just created.

Typed rather than a bare `serde_json::Value`, because the id is the whole
point of the call: "create this person and assign the shot to them" is one
user action, and a client that cannot read the id back has to re-list every
person and match on the name to find what it just made.

id.description: Generated person id, ready to be used as a `person_id` anywhere.

name.description: The name as stored — trimmed, which may differ from what was sent.

removed.description: Faces removed — or, for a dry run, faces that would be removed.

source_file_id.description: Optional: specific file to use as source. If omitted, the original file is used.

source_mode.description:
Which part of a video source to feed the workflow: `first_frame`,
`last_frame`, `at_time:<ms>`, `keyframe:<n>` or `whole_video`.

Omit it to let the workflow decide — a graph with a video loader takes
the whole clip, anything else takes the first frame. Ignored for stills.

FaceSuggestion.description:
Get suggested persons for a face based on embedding similarity.

Computes cosine similarity on-the-fly between the target face and the
thumbnail face of every person, so results are always up-to-date even
for newly created persons.

synthetic.description:
Made by a machine rather than a camera. `GET /api/files/{id}/manifest`
says how.

FileManifestResponse.description: What a file says about where it came from.

oneOf.description:
How it was made. Absent for a photograph, and for a generated file that
predates provenance being recorded — a library can hold variants created
before anyone wrote down where they came from.

manifest_error.description:
Present when a stored manifest could not be read back. The raw text is
returned rather than dropped: unreadable provenance is still evidence.

manifest_raw.description: The stored manifest exactly as written, when it would not parse.

synthetic.description: Whether a machine made this picture rather than a camera.

IngestStatus.description:
What the queue is doing for one library, for the import UI to poll.

[`completed`] and [`failed`] count since the server started, not since the
current upload: the client knows how many files it sent, and the pair of
numbers it cares about — how many are still coming and whether any broke —
are both derivable from these without the server tracking upload sessions.

analyzing.description: Files being analyzed right now (0 or 1 — one worker per library).

failed.description: Files whose analysis failed since startup. They stay on disk.

MergePeoplePayload.description: Merge two people: move all faces from source to target, then delete source

MergeShotsPayload.description: POST /api/shots/merge - move all files from source to target shot. Delete source.

OrganizeStatsResponse.description: Return detailed organize stats about the library

PersonFaceBrief.description: Get up to 12 face IDs with thumbnail URLs for a person

PersonMeta.description:
Browse a person: returns person metadata + all shots + all files per shot.
Solves the N+1 problem for the mobile client.

ProvenanceManifest.description: How a generated file came to exist.

comfyui_prompt_id.description:
ComfyUI's own id for the run, which is how its history can still be
matched up if the server keeps it.

compiled_prompt.description: The prompt as submitted, after every override was applied.

generated_at.description: When Phos brought the file into the library, UTC, `YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS`.

line_id.description: The generation line this file belongs to.

output_filename.description:
The name ComfyUI gave the output, before Phos renamed it into the
library — the last thread back to the run that made it.

seed.description: The seed the sampler actually ran with.

source_file_id.description: The library file the run was given to work from, when there was one.

stage_index.description: Position of this run in a multi-stage line, zero-based.

text_overrides.description: The text the user put into the workflow, node id → prompt.

version.description: Which shape of this record was written. See [`MANIFEST_VERSION`].

additionalProperties.description:
Anything a newer Phos wrote that this one has no field for. Kept so a
round trip through an older binary does not quietly drop provenance.

Flattened, so it has no name of its own in the JSON and nothing to
publish in the schema — a client generated from an older spec simply
does not see the newer keys, which is the point.

ReassignFacePayload.description: Reassign a face to a different person

access_key.description: The S3 access key id (OIDC sub in multi-user mode, "phos" in single-user).

bucket.description: The fixed bucket name the library is exposed as.

endpoint.description: External endpoint URL override (PHOS_S3_PUBLIC_URL), if configured.

secret_key.description:
The secret key. Stored in plaintext server-side because SigV4 signing
requires the real secret; only returned to the authenticated owner.

SessionClaims.description: JWT claims for the user session cookie.

synthetic.description:
The shot's main file was made by a machine. The card says so, because
the picture itself cannot.

SplitShotPayload.description:
POST /api/shots/:id/split - create new shot from specified files.
New shot inherits primary person from faces. Both shots get review_status = 'pending'.

StatsResponse.description: Return aggregate stats about the library

TokenResponse.description: Response containing a Phos session JWT.

UpdateShotPayload.description:
PUT /api/shots/:id - update primary_person_id and/or review_status.
When primary_person changes, assign new folder_number (MAX+1 for that person).

username.description: The WebDAV username (OIDC sub in multi-user mode, "phos" in single-user).

session_cookie.description: Session JWT set as HttpOnly cookie (phos_session) after OIDC login
